native_access_review.method: Read-only comparison of frozen native-v1 to the previously reviewed core; actual public native test assertions and owner logs inspected.
reviewed_behavior: Owned browser pages use a chosen save destination before accepting a download; tracked downloads are bounded at eight, completed entries are removed, and owner shutdown cancels remaining requests.
Supported site permissions display their requesting HTTP(S) origin and purpose as plain text; No is the default and escape choice; unsupported capabilities are denied.

One permission dialog is bound to the exact page/instance, generation and URL. Navigation, close, crash and owner shutdown retire it. A retired permission answer does not change the origin's stored choice.

Filesystem requests show the local chosen path, requesting origin, file/folder kind and read/write access. They require explicit Allow; denial or retirement rejects access. The existing upload picker is retained.
Remote pages retain separate managed profiles and do not receive the local shell WebChannel or a debugging endpoint.
limits: The eight-download bound was inspected in code; the added native fixture exercises a chosen export destination, not eight simultaneous transfers.
Native fixtures exercise actual Qt WebEngine requests and Qt dialogs, with the platform-native dialog presentation disabled only in the fixture so choices can be automated.
Anonymous Office/VS Code smoke, the root full-tree release gate, Windows deployment, ZIP verification and reload are separate root/owner work; no completion claim is made here.
Desktop/screen capture is intentionally unsupported until a screen chooser can show the actual requested access.
